To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ontologies can be represented as partially ordered sets, (2) clustering algorithms do not necessarily produce ontologies, and (3) a clustering algorithm that produces ontologies can be derived from a dissimililarity matrix.

(1) classical clustering algorithms cannot preserve arbitrary pairwise dissimilarities, and (2) we propose a clustering algorithm that can preserve arbitrary pairwise dissimilarity, and can be used to generate ontologies.

(i) classical clustering algorithms do not preserve all information contained in dissimilarity matrices; (ii) the space of ontological representations of a dissimilarity data matrix is a partially ordered set over the subset relation; and (iii) the new clustering algorithm preserves all information contained in the dissimilarity matrix.
